scientific_object: retrospective active-learning simulation on public experimental antibody-binding landscapes
chronology: freeze source identities, candidate assays, acquisition rules, prediction, model, budgets, seeds, and scoring
run every assay-strategy-seed unit without inspecting partial comparative outcomes
verify the complete unit matrix and exact source identities
open and score comparative outcomes only after the release gate passes

prediction.rule: maximize predictive mean plus one predictive standard deviation
prediction.origin: a four-target ligand-binding audit selected a balanced UCB schedule, and an external two-landscape Rubisco audit preserved the UCB-over-random direction
prediction.claim_boundary: one frozen acquisition choice, not a universal ordering of active-learning strategies

strategies.ucb: largest predictive mean plus one predictive standard deviation
strategies.thompson: largest draw from the predictive normal approximation

model.representation: outcome-blind 256-dimensional character 1--3-gram hashing of concatenated heavy and light chains
model.rationale: a simple ensemble supplies the mean and uncertainty required by all five acquisition rules without target-specific tuning

evaluation.primary_curve: recall of the full assay's top-2% variants after each observed batch
evaluation.primary_utility: trapezoidal area under the recall curve, normalized over the observed-count interval
evaluation.endpoint_sensitivity: top-2% recall after the final batch

primary: mean normalized allocation regret of the frozen UCB choice across assays
UCB pairwise win credit against the four alternative strategies

prohibitions: inspecting partial comparative outcomes before the complete-matrix gate passes
changing the selected strategy or model after outcome-bearing execution begins
dropping assays or seeds based on their outcomes
describing the public-data simulation as prospective wet-lab evidence
